In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
children's problems in processing patient initial sentences is due to the interaction of frequency and incremental processing.

the child's difficulty in processing patient initial sentences is due to the interaction of several factors including frequency of use, processing complexity and the child's knowledge of language structure and use.
children's difficulty in interpreting patient-initial sentences is not a general phenomenon, but a language specific phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the processing of patient-initial sentences in Tagalog is more difficult for young children compared to adults, but this difficulty is mitigated by the use of morphosyntactic voice markers.
the use of word order and voice markers is an effective strategy for children to acquire thematic roles.
the frequency account and the incremental processing model are both valid in explaining children's difficulty in interpreting passive sentences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of thematic roles in Tagalog is affected by both word order and morphological markers.
children's difficulties in interpreting passive sentences are not due to the lack of a reliable cue to thematic role assignment, as is often the case in English.
even though the dominant order in Tagalog is agent initial, children's performance is still affected by the frequency of patient initial sentences.
